_note: Real FIM alert for Scripts/linux-simulations.sh persistence, run on 2026-08-27. The persistence technique originally targeted the user's personal crontab (/var/spool/cron/crontabs), but this host's FIM only watches /etc, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /bin, /sbin, /boot by default - the technique was switched to write /etc/cron.d/update-check instead, already covered under the monitored /etc tree. Getting a real alert also required understanding a genuine Wazuh FIM behavior: the scan immediately following any wazuh-agent daemon restart is always treated as a fresh baseline and never generates alerts, regardless of whether the underlying FIM database already has history - restarting the agent to force a rescan (the first approach tried) silently absorbed the new file into the baseline instead of alerting on it. The fix was to shorten the scan frequency (43200s -> 30s), let the daemon settle into genuine periodic (non-restart-triggered) scans, and only then create the file - that's the alert captured here, decoder syscheck_integrity_changed, real checksums included. Captured verbatim via `docker exec single-node-wazuh.manager-1 grep "100210" /var/ossec/logs/alerts/alerts.json`, no content altered.
